title: Leaf removal
what: Pulling leaves from the fruit zone to bare the bunches: which side, and when (early, from fruit set to bunch closure, or late, around véraison).
choose: An open fruit zone dries faster: less botrytis, better spray cover. The morning side is the safe one; the afternoon side takes the hottest sun. Go early: berries exposed from fruit set acclimatise, while baring shade-grown fruit before a heatwave is the classic sunburn case.
exam: Expect 'explain how canopy management affects grape quality' for a named grape. Chain exposure → grape compounds → aroma, and weigh the sunburn risk.

check.question: A dense Napa Cabernet canopy at the start of véraison, with a heatwave forecast. The crew proposes stripping both sides now to cut green-pepper notes. Your answer?
options: No: pyrazine levels are largely set before véraison, and baring shade-grown fruit now invites sunburn
Yes: sun from now on breaks down most of the pyrazines
Yes, but only the morning side: gentle sun now still lowers the pyrazines
Yes: late removal acclimatises the berries best
check.answer: No: pyrazine levels are largely set before véraison, and baring shade-grown fruit now invites sunburn
check.why: Light before véraison decides most of the IBMP that accumulates; exposure afterwards does little. Berries grown in shade burn at a lower surface temperature than acclimatised ones.
